question: Under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), who is primarily responsible for completing the S-form (syndromic surveillance report)?

answers.text: District epidemiologist at the District Health Office

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: District epidemiologists compile and analyse data but do not complete the S-form at source.

answers.text: Community health workers such as ASHAs and ANMs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The S-form (syndromic) is completed by community health workers — ASHAs and ANMs — who report syndromes (e.g., fever with rash, acute diarrhoea) from the community level.
Private hospitals may contribute to P-form (presumptive) and L-form (laboratory) reporting, but the S-form is primarily a community-level tool completed by ASHAs/ANMs.
Laboratory technicians complete the L-form (laboratory-confirmed). The S-form is for syndromic reporting by community health workers.

overallFeedback.feedback: The IDSP S-form (syndromic) is completed by community health workers — ASHAs and ANMs — representing the first tier of the surveillance pyramid.
Well done! ASHAs and ANMs complete the IDSP S-form at the community level for syndromic surveillance.
